subject: URGENT: CareChat streaming p99 surge during peak - SSE / WebSocket impacts
messages:
From: Lucy Chen <lucy@carechat.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@carechat.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SR#7891 — Streaming p99 spikes at peak (SSE)

Hi Olga,

We started seeing a sustained p99 latency increase on the streaming chat endpoint (SSE) during our 5pm PST peak. This began around 16:50 PST and persists — it affects about 12% of connections and causes timeouts in our client. Error traces show a mix of 504s and client disconnects.

Quick data:
- Peak window: ~16:50–17:10 PST
- Observed p95: 1.1s -> 1.4s (baseline 0.9s)
- Observed p99: 2.7s -> 6.8s
- Throughput: +38% vs baseline (more concurrent users)

We've attached a short CSV with sample request_ids and a screenshot of our dashboard. We can provide longer traces if you need them. This is impacting two enterprise customers in our test cohort and a small but revenue-sensitive subset of active users.

Can your team patch or give a mitigation plan? If you need us to shift traffic temporarily, we can throttle a subset of clients.

Thanks,
Lucy
Account Lead — CareChat
--
Attachment: carechat-ticket-7891.pdf (summary), sample-reqs.csv

What we’ll do first:
- Dylan will pull server-side traces and check queue/backpressure metrics for SSE workers.
- We’ll compare the active model variants and see if fallback routing kicked in.
- If needed, we can enable short-term burst capacity for your dedicated pool.

I’ll keep you updated every 60–90 minutes until we have a mitigation.

—Olga

olga_petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, Lucy Chen <lucy@carechat.ai>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:47 -0800
Subject: Re: SR#7891 — Streaming p99 spikes at peak (SSE)

Quick triage update:
- Observed: a subset (~15%) of SSE worker pods in us-west-2 are showing sustained CPU at ~92% and a backlog on the internal request queue; most affected nodes host the streaming routing layer (SSE proxy + KV cache).
- Logs indicate increased handshake retries and some long tail GC in a small subset of pods.
- I’ve pulled a short set of traces (attached: sse-traces-20261130.zip) showing several requests with large wait times in the pre-handler queue.

Immediate mitigations I’m recommending now:
1) Increase SSE worker replica target by +30% for the next 90 minutes in the us-west-2 pool (manual scale).
2) Temporarily divert lower-priority traffic to a cheaper routing path (we have a model-variant fallback ready).
3) Disable a recent experimental batching change for streaming that was rolled out to 10% last week (possible regression).

I’ll open a quick runbook step and start the scale-up if I get a green from Markus or Neha for the capacity burst.

—Dylan
SRE — Redwood Inference
Attachment: sse-traces-20261130.zip, grafana-p99-20261130.png
